messages:
jordan: quick thread — stage gate numbers for bringing up Mistral-13B + Llama-2-13B. ran short prefills (1k tokens) and decode slices (200 tokens) across A100/H100 in us-east1 + eu-west1, q4 vs q8x4. TL;DR: A100 surprisingly better on prefill p50 for long contexts; H100 wins steady-state decode tokens/sec. cost tradeoffs depend on batch and kv-hit.

sam: can you paste the raw numbers? especially p95/p99 and $/1M tokens.

jordan: sure — grabbing the CI summary. note: these are isolated infra runs (no burst), 1 GPU each, same model weights and quant pipeline.

ci-bot: automated-run: m13b_vs_l2_13b | regions: [us-east1, eu-west1] | skus: [a100-80gb, h100-80gb] | quant: [q4, q8x4] | batch_sizes: [1,4,8] | kv_hit: [0%, 50%]

ci-bot: results CSV:
```
model,sku,region,phase,quant,batch,kv_hit,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,tokens_per_sec,dollars_per_1M
mistral-13b,a100,us-east1,prefill,q4,1,0,210,480,860,220,9.6
mistral-13b,h100,us-east1,prefill,q4,1,0,260,540,980,180,11.3
mistral-13b,a100,us-east1,decode,q4,1,0,12,48,140,220,9.6
mistral-13b,h100,us-east1,decode,q4,1,0,9,36,120,285,7.5
mistral-13b,a100,eu-west1,prefill,q8x4,4,50,190,430,820,260,8.8
mistral-13b,h100,eu-west1,prefill,q8x4,4,50,220,490,1100,210,10.1
llama2-13b,a100,us-east1,decode,q8x4,8,50,14,60,180,240,8.4
llama2-13b,h100,us-east1,decode,q8x4,8,50,10,40,150,310,6.9
```

lee: ok interesting — A100 is ~1.25x better on prefill p50 in most shots (esp q4). do we think this is memory-bandwidth / contiguous memcpy behavior on long prefill?

ana: (I'm ana) we saw that before — prefill favors A100 on long sequences for some model kernels because H100's tensor cores are optimized for small-matrix matmuls in decode; prefill is big matmul with kv assembly. also our kernel selector chose different matmul codepaths: `gemm_split` on a100 vs `tensor_fuse` on h100 for that sequence length.

jordan: yes — kernel mix note: 
```
A100 prefill: fused-gemm -> continuous-batch path
H100 prefill: tensor-fuse w/ split-buffer (higher overhead at long seq)
```

sam: eu-west1 had higher p99 on H100, any infra notes?

ops-bot: infra alert: eu-west1-h100 rack 3 reported 5% thermal-throttle events during continuous 2-hour runs (sustained prefill load). fallback activated: reduced boost clocks -> +15% latency at p95.

lee: that matches the p99 delta — H100 thermal behavior increased tail risk in eu-west1 on sustained prefill workloads. worth flagging to capacity planning for region sizing.

ana: on decode tokens/sec the H100 wins ~1.2-1.3x (see tokens_per_sec). that reduces $/1M tokens for h100 on decode-heavy workloads — see llama2 rows. but on mixed prefills (long context) the A100 overall $/1M can be better because prefill cost dominates token budget.

jordan: actionable takeaways for the stage-gate checklist: 
- mark model as "prefill-sensitive"; prefer A100 in regions where customers do long-context system prompts.
- prefer H100 for low-latency decode-only chat workloads (short context, high qps).
- add kernel-selector override in model profile to force `fused-gemm` on H100 for seq>1k as an experiment.
- add thermal soak test in eu-west1 to catch throttle-induced tail regressions.

sam: can we estimate capacity sizing impact? if a customer has 30% prefill heavy traffic, how to pick sku?

jordan: rough example from these numbers (per-1M tokens cost split by phase): 
```
scenario A (30% prefill long): A100 overall $/1M ~ 8.9, H100 overall $/1M ~ 9.8
scenario B (5% prefill): A100 $/1M ~ 8.2, H100 $/1M ~ 7.1
```

ana: so guidance: for product teams that have >20% long-prefill share, recommend A100 reservation; otherwise H100 makes sense. also recommend q8x4 for decoding-heavy to balance quality/cost.

lee: let's not forget kv-hit effects — with 50% kv_hit tokens_per_sec improves and prefill cost amortizes. our CSV includes some 50% hits; maybe run targeted 80% hit to model CDN cache effects.

ci-bot: queued follow-up: run 80% kv_hit sweep + kernel-override on H100 next night. estimated run time 6h.

sam: nice. can we add a short blurb for the onboarding doc: two bullets (1) prefill vs decode SKU guidance, (2) region thermal soak requirement. I'll PR. :+1:

jordan: cool — i'll open the PR and link these outputs + raw csv. thanks all.

ops-bot: deploy-bench: archived results -> s3://redwood-ml-bench/m13b_stagegate/1768009999/results.csv

ana: one last note — quality regression check: q4 vs q8x4 diffs small on our eval set, but run offline eval on customer prompts before final rollout.

lee: agreed. end of thread.
